AK.key_factor: Ranked-choice transfers from Republican Gerald Heikes and same-name candidate Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. should favor Sullivan, likely offsetting Peltola's roughly 2-point first-choice polling lead, which was measured before the Oct. 28 spoiler-recruitment story.
AK.reasoning: Peltola led most first-choice polls by 1-7 points and outraised Sullivan 2.6 to 1 in a strongly Democratic year. But roughly 5% of first choices will likely go to Heikes and Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., whose transfers should favor Sullivan. Alaska polls have often understated Republicans, and the spoiler-recruitment story, with state and federal investigations, hit Peltola in the final week. Shares shown are first-choice: I expect a near-tie there and a narrow Sullivan win after tabulation.

FL.key_factor: Moody has led nearly every poll, by about 6 points on average, and Florida polls have understated Republicans in each of the last four cycles.
FL.reasoning: Moody faces a progressive nominee in an R+13 state and leads the polling average by about 6. Democrats reached rough parity with Republicans in early ballots by registration, a sign of the national swing. But Republicans hold a 1.5 million registration edge and usually dominate Election Day voting. I expect a margin far below Rubio's 16 points in 2022 but still comfortable for Moody.

IA.key_factor: The polls are essentially tied, and Iowa polls have understated Republicans in nearly every recent cycle, including the 2018 Democratic wave.
IA.reasoning: More than 30 polls average roughly even, and Turek's large money and outside-spending advantages keep him competitive in a strongly Democratic year. But Iowa polls underestimated Ernst in 2020, Reynolds in 2018 and Trump in 2024. The state's R+13 baseline still implies a modest Republican edge even in a D+8 national environment. Hinson by 2 to 3 points, with Laehn near 2%.

KS.key_factor: Every nonpartisan poll fielded since Trump's Oct. 20 rally for Marshall shows Hamilton ahead, by 3 to 9 points.
KS.reasoning: Marshall is damaged by reporting that he sued more than 700 patients, trails badly in fundraising, and the latest Emerson, SSRS and Washington Post polls all put Hamilton ahead. But Kansas federal polling has understated Republicans before (Roberts in 2014, Marshall in 2020). Undecided Republicans may come home, and Kansas has not elected a Democratic senator since 1932, so I discount the lead to under 2 points.

ME.key_factor: Jackson leads by 2 to 3 points in October polling, but Collins trailed in nearly every 2020 poll and still won by 8.6 points.
ME.reasoning: In a D+8 midterm, Maine's partisan baseline is roughly D+17, yet Collins runs close, a measure of her personal brand. Jackson leads most October polls narrowly, and midterm polling has generally lacked the Republican-understating errors of presidential years. Against that, Collins has beaten her polls in recent races, most dramatically in 2020. The wave and the ProPublica pay-to-play story give Jackson the slightest edge in a genuine coin flip.

MI.key_factor: El-Sayed leads by 5 to 8 points in nearly every late-October poll, including Rasmussen's.
MI.reasoning: El-Sayed's lead widened in October to about 5 points, and a D+8 environment favors Democrats in a state Trump carried by 1.4. But Michigan Senate polls overstated Democrats in 2018, 2020 and 2024, and Rogers nearly won in 2024. Republican-side outside spending is also more than double the Democratic side's, so I trim the lead to about 3.5 points. El-Sayed is a clear but not safe favorite.

MN.key_factor: Flanagan leads every poll, and Minnesota's Democratic lean is amplified by a D+8 national environment.
MN.reasoning: Flanagan's lead grew from a September tie in SurveyUSA's polling to 7 points in late October, with NYT/Siena at 14. Minnesota polls have been fairly accurate, and a generic Democrat should win comfortably here in this environment. Tafoya's celebrity and Trump's late endorsement have not closed the gap: even her campaign's own poll showed her down 4. Flanagan by about 8.

NC.key_factor: Cooper has led every poll by 5 to 14 points, and registered Democrats outnumbered Republicans 925,000 to 604,000 among early voters.
NC.reasoning: A two-term former governor faces the former RNC chair in a D+8 year with a wide money advantage. Recent Republican-sponsored polls show Cooper up 8 to 10, and the Senate Leadership Fund canceled about $30 million planned for Whatley. North Carolina polls have modestly understated Republicans, but not by nearly enough to matter. Cooper by about 10.

NE.key_factor: Ricketts leads the polling average by about a point, and Osborn lost by 6.7 in 2024 after polls showed a closer race.
NE.reasoning: Osborn's populist independent campaign, Democratic backing and a D+8 environment make this competitive in an R+20 state, and outside money favors him. But Republican polls show Ricketts up 3 to 5, and Osborn's own campaign poll had him down 2. Ricketts is also a better-funded, higher-profile incumbent than Fischer was. Expect Ricketts by about 3, with minor candidates near 3%.

NH.key_factor: Pappas has led every poll since mid-September by 5 to 8 points, in a state Democrats should carry comfortably in a D+8 year.
NH.reasoning: The Sununu family brand keeps John E. Sununu closer than the partisan baseline. But he has trailed consistently, including in Republican-sponsored polls, and was outraised about four to one. New Hampshire's 2022 midterm polls understated Democrats. Pappas by about 7.

OH.key_factor: Brown leads the polling average by about 3.5 points, but Ohio polls have understated Republicans in most recent cycles.
OH.reasoning: Brown has led nearly every poll since September, holds a large money advantage and runs well ahead of his party. A D+8 environment also erases much of Ohio's R+11 tilt. But Ohio polls overstated Brown in both 2018 and 2024, and the state has moved right, so I trim his lead to under 2 points. Lean Brown in a close race.

SC.key_factor: South Carolina's R+18 baseline and a history of polls understating Republicans outweigh Darline Graham's weak campaign.
SC.reasoning: Polls average Graham about +2, with NYT/Siena tied, and Andrews has a roughly 12-to-1 fundraising edge over an appointed, little-known incumbent. But Lindsey Graham won by 10 in 2020 after polls showed a close race, and later SC polls also understated Republicans. Undecideds, like the Citadel's 15%, should lean Republican. Graham by about 4 or 5.

TX.key_factor: Talarico leads most of 55 polls, by about 3 points on average and including several from Republican-aligned pollsters, against a scandal-plagued nominee.
TX.reasoning: Paxton's impeachment history, refusal to debate and six-to-one fundraising deficit erase much of Texas's usual Republican edge, and a D+8 environment helps Talarico. Texas polls understated Republicans in 2020 and 2024 but understated Democrats in the 2018 midterm wave. The state's voter-registration backlog adds downside risk. Talarico by about 2.

upset_watch.why: Collins trailed in nearly every 2020 poll and won by 8.6 points, so repeating even part of that overperformance would erase Jackson's narrow lead.
